page: Microsoft Azure FX96mds_v2 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. It features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1832.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 19.08 GB of memory per core. Additionally, the instance includes 5669 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage configurations.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 103610.4 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 97945.78. Memory performance is a key highlight, achieving top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 7620.93 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth of 188.83 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier PassMark database score of 37422.58 and Redis SET performance reaching 130.32 million operations per second. The processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 support contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks, including LLM inference prompt processing for a medium 7B model at 319.65 tokens per second.

From a resource density perspective, the FX96mds_v2 provides a high ratio of memory and local storage relative to its vCPU count, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets without the overhead of external storage. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 2169.79, indicating that workloads bound strictly by single-threaded execution speed may not fully leverage this hardware profile.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and memory-bound data processing pipelines.
